rationale: Ownership is unchanged (selection.json, revision fc9ec3b1, no bundles installed): communication_kernel_sum_ms is generated exclusively by the 13 fp32 c10d::allreduce_ bucket calls of DDP's final-micro-batch reducer - call d0938de87369efd500322679 (12 buckets x 7,087,872 elements = 28,351,488 B) and call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b (one 157,541,376 B bucket) - both direct children of the single complete-workload project call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb); execution_timeline-1221e205 and nsys-9ed9145c show exactly 13 NCCL kernels and no other NCCL device work. How previous-feedback.txt changes this attempt: it contains the measured failure of the last trial (trial-f684195486, revision 43b0f446...). That candidate had this same single direct project.invoke boundary and plan, but its CUDA graph capture of the no_sync micro-batches died in the parent's own forward at transformers 5.16.1 masking_utils.py:603 (eager_mask): torch.where(mask, torch.tensor(0.0, device=mask.device, dtype=dtype), min_dtype) raises 'Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA graph capture unless the CPU tensor is pinned' because torch.tensor(..., device=cuda) builds a pageable CPU scalar and copies it host-to-device inside capture. Both ranks fell back to the parent on every invocation (route fallback:parent:capture_failed:RuntimeError, corroborated by candidate_diagnostics-4123e6d6 exception evidence), the objective regressed to 73.14 vs reference 66.55 (endpoint kernel sums 65.19/81.10, paired gains 2.40/-15.59 below the 2.58/4.54 ms MAD noise bounds) and the step constraint failed (145.55/144.25 vs limit 144.80321415). The concrete repair, verified against the worker's installed stack (transformers 5.16.1, torch 2.13.0+cu129): the captured segments call the underlying module with an explicit precomputed 4D causal attention mask, and transformers 5.16.1 masking_utils._preprocess_mask_arguments returns an already-prepared 4D mask as-is (create_causal_mask early exit), so eager_mask and its uncapturable torch.tensor(0.0, device=cuda) are never executed inside capture while the eager attention path computes the identical attn_weights + mask addition. The constructed mask is torch.equal to create_causal_mask's own output for the parent's calls (attention_mask=None, no cache, no padding), and the masked forward reproduces the parent forward's loss, logits and every gradient bit-exactly; both checks now run inside the candidate too (per live inputs, before any capture attempt, aborting to a labeled parent fallback on mismatch). Each segment additionally executes eagerly once on a side stream with primed in-place gradient buffers before capture, so library lazy init and eager-side failures surface outside the capture region and leave no half-captured allocator state (unlike the previous attempt, whose failure surfaced mid-capture). The rest is the previously designed and now re-verified execution policy: first invocation runs the pure parent reference (bucket rebuild, warmup, exact outputs for the correctness pass); the second invocation - an untimed warmup under the documented harness order (correctness pass, warmup 2, 5 clean timed repeats, 3 separately profiled samples, inventory pass) - validates the mask path, performs the side-stream warmup, captures one graph per no_sync micro-batch into one shared pool (replayed in capture order), and finishes that invocation through replay plus the eager final micro-batch; every later invocation is replay-only. Per invocation the static input buffers are refreshed from the current inputs and gradients accumulate in place into persistent per-parameter buffers primed and zeroed before each replay, so the workload executes on current inputs every invocation; the final synchronized micro-batch runs eagerly through the unmodified DDP wrapper (reducer, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True, default NCCL process group, all 13 bucket allreduces untouched), followed by the SGD step and single final torch.cuda.synchronize, with optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) inside the timed boundary exactly as the parent. Numerical equivalence was re-established by measurement on two-rank gloo DDP on CPU with the actual installed transformers: the full chain (mask-passthrough segments into primed zeroed buffers + eager final micro through DDP + SGD step) reproduces the parent step's total loss, all four micro losses, every gradient and every post-step parameter bit-exactly, and candidate gradients are identical across ranks (exact_gradient_replica_check uses atol=0.0/rtol=0.0), so global_batch_gradient_check, parameter_update_check, finite_loss and the corruption control behave as baseline. Expected effects, from measured records: replay makes the CPU dispatch of the three no_sync micro-batches near-constant and early on both ranks, removing the measured 10.34-10.67 ms cross-rank CPU submit spread and the rank-0 first-kernel absorption (+1.4/+1.5/+4.7 ms over samples), so both ranks enter the 13-collective burst nearly aligned; the max-rank kernel sum should move from the baseline samples 63.21/63.32/66.48 and 63.41/63.67/64.12 (parent endpoint 66.548 ms last AB/BA) toward the collective_calibration-1af5837f warmed floor 61.82 ms (rank 0) / 62.90 ms (rank 1), i.e. an expected paired gain of roughly 0.4-4.5 ms depending on which parent endpoint noise is drawn. Step time should also fall well inside the constraint because replay removes rather than adds CPU dispatch work (parent AB/BA 139.96/146.20 ms, limit 144.80 ms), replacing the marginal-failure regime of the fallback-running previous trial. Alternatives remain evidence-barred, not merely untried: functional binding of the two allreduce_ sites under the fixed legacy backend costs +92.3/+100.8 ms clean step time (binding_cost-2087a4f7); a gloo barrier before the burst propagated release skew into the remaining launches (rank-0 kernel sums 80.5/73.9/81.1 ms in trial-43f18a5360); communicator rerouting and NCCL env forcing are provider configuration and lost the step constraint anyway (trial-5a705e709d, 253.9-295.5 ms); precision or byte reduction fails grad_atol=1e-6/grad_rtol=1e-4. Honest unknowns to be measured, not assumed: whether rank 1's +0.77 ms mid-burst excess above its floor is CPU-launch-side (addressable here) or transport jitter/SM contention that no in-contract scheduling change removes, in which case this run acts as a measured control that pins the in-contract floor; whether the expected gain clears the MAD-derived noise bounds (2.58/4.54 ms last round); and whether any GPU-only capture hazard outside the now-fixed masking path remains - any such failure degrades permanently and safely to the parent reference with distinct labels, never re-running the collective-bearing final micro-batch.

setup_work.build_time: build(context) is installation only: it resolves the project.invoke boundary from context['targets']/'references', validates that the state carries a DDP model, the underlying module, an SGD optimizer and at least two input micro-batches on a CUDA worker, and returns the single replacement mapping. No GPU work, no collectives, no parameter or data transformation, no allocation happens at build time; an empty mapping is returned if any guard fails (e.g. a non-CPU worker).
setup_work.capture_timing: Lazy setup inside actual adapter execution, per the binding contract (the raw parent is never called at installation; the first replacement call runs the parent reference in the adapter's real invocation context). Invocation 1 (the correctness pass) runs the pure parent reference via context['references'], completing DDP's one-time bucket rebuild, library warmup and exact outputs. Invocation 2 - an untimed warmup under the documented harness order (correctness, warmup 2, 5 timed repeats, 3 profiled samples, inventory; warmup precedes every timed or profiled invocation) - performs the graph setup: (a) builds the 4D causal mask (a few KiB, shape (1,1,seq,seq) fp32) outside capture; (b) validates mask-path bit-exactness on the live current inputs with two no_grad forwards compared by torch.equal (loss and logits), aborting to a labeled parent fallback before any capture attempt on mismatch; (c) primes per-parameter gradient buffers (about 497.8 MB fp32 for GPT-2 124M, one persistent tensor per parameter) and warms each segment eagerly once on a side stream with the exact captured call (masked forward + scaled backward, in-place accumulation into the primed buffers); (d) re-zeros the buffers and captures one CUDA graph per no_sync micro-batch into one shared pool (torch.cuda.graph performs its documented synchronize and empty_cache around each capture; graphs are always replayed in capture order, the documented safe pattern for a shared pool); (e) verifies the in-place accumulation flavor (parameter.grad is buffer for every parameter, else a distinct setup failure label aborts); (f) finishes that invocation through replays plus the eager final micro-batch, SGD step and synchronize, returning the normal result structure. Every later invocation - timed repeats, the 3 separately profiled diagnostic samples and the comm-hook inventory pass - is replay-only: refresh static input buffers from the current inputs, zero and re-prime the buffers, replay the three graphs, run the final micro-batch eagerly through the unmodified DDP reducer (its comm-hook inventory still observes the same 13 buckets), then the optimizer step and the single final torch.cuda.synchronize. The held-out longer_sequence variant (sequence_length=256, accumulation_steps=2) captures its own shapes in its own worker process; nothing fixture-dependent is cached, since each replay reads the current input buffers and the current in-place parameter storage.
setup_work.memory: Setup allocation is explicit: one retained gradient-buffer set of 124,439,808 fp32 elements (about 497.8 MB) held for the process lifetime, three static input clones (a few KiB), three 4D masks (a few hundred KiB total), plus the CUDA graph pool holding the captured segments' persistent intermediates and static losses (raises reserved memory; exact size observed at validation). torch.cuda.graph's documented synchronize and empty_cache run once per capture, inside the untimed warmup invocation, not between timed runs. Warm-run peak_allocated_bytes may stay near baseline or fall slightly because the parent's per-step autograd gradient allocations are replaced by the retained buffers and pool allocations - this is a counter/lifetime effect, not a claimed physical-memory saving; framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes include the capture invocation by definition and will rise with the retained pools. If the graph path aborts at any stage, the buffers and partial graphs are dropped from the book and the process degrades to the parent path, which re-establishes its own allocator behavior from the next invocation.
setup_work.state_lifecycle_and_synchronization: reset() reloads weights in place (load_state_dict copies into the same parameter storage the graphs read), so replay-based invocations start from the correct weights without recapture; gradients are cleared inside the timed invocation exactly as the parent (optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True), then the primed buffers are zeroed by one fused foreach zero of about 497.8 MB, well under 1 ms); SGD has momentum 0.0 so there is no optimizer state; the only device synchronization inside the timed step remains the parent's single final torch.cuda.synchronize. No barrier, no extra collective, no comm hook, no environment variable and no process-group change is introduced anywhere; the gloo control-group barrier in before_run stays outside the replacement; the DDP reducer, its bucket configuration, the default NCCL process group and all 13 bucket allreduces are untouched, so the inventory_hook diagnostic pass still records the same bucket counts and logical bytes. Affected scope is the whole bundle group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb, replaced at its root project call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0; both ranks install the same replacement and keep identical collective sequences per invocation even under asymmetric failure (three no_sync micro-batches plus one synchronized final backward), so collective participation and ordering are preserved on all ranks.
setup_work.route_labels: context['record_route'] is bound with context.get('record_route') or a no-op lambda and invoked inside the replacement on the chosen path: eager:parent:first_invocation (first call, pure parent reference), capture:mask_passthrough_graphs+eager_final_micro (warmup invocation that captured and replayed), replay:mask_passthrough_graphs+eager_final_micro (steady state), and distinct fallback labels separating unsupported signature (fallback:parent:unsupported_signature), model replacement (fallback:parent:model_replaced), steady state after a failure (fallback:parent:steady_state:<reason>), setup-stage failures before any capture attempt (fallback:parent:setup_failed:mask_not_bit_exact, setup_failed:mask_check_error:<Exc>, setup_failed:warmup_failed:<Exc>), capture-stage failure (fallback:parent:capture_failed:<Exc>) and runtime replay failure including workload-shape change (fallback:parent:replay_failed:<Exc>). Labels are diagnostic self-report only; output, coverage and trace evidence remain the framework's checks.

quality_risks: Mask-passthrough equivalence is verified, not assumed: the constructed 4D mask is bit-equal to transformers 5.16.1 create_causal_mask's output for the parent's calls on the installed stack, and the masked forward reproduces loss, logits and all gradients bit-exactly. The candidate re-verifies loss/logits bit-equality on the live inputs at the start of the capture invocation; any mismatch aborts the graph path before any capture attempt and routes the process permanently through the parent with label fallback:parent:setup_failed:mask_not_bit_exact, so outputs can only ever come from an verified-equivalent path or the parent itself.

Capture legality and fallback: the known capture killer of the previous trial (eager_mask's unpinned CPU-scalar copy, masking_utils.py:603) is structurally bypassed by the 4D passthrough, and the exact captured code path is executed eagerly on a side stream before capture so lazy init and eager-side failures surface outside the capture region. If any other uncapturable operation appears, the exception permanently disables the graph path and routes that and all later invocations through the parent reference; gradients and weights are left in a state the parent's zero_grad(set_to_none=True) fully resets, so the fallback invocation is exactly the parent step. The collective-bearing final micro-batch and the optimizer step are never re-run by a fallback, so a mid-invocation failure cannot desynchronize the two ranks' collectives; even an asymmetric failure (graphs succeeding on one rank only) leaves both ranks performing three no_sync micro-batches plus one synchronized final backward with the same 13 allreduces per invocation, so there is no deadlock or collective mismatch by construction.

Accumulation flavor: replay requires the captured backward to accumulate in place into the primed buffers; this is verified immediately after capture (parameter.grad is buffer for every parameter, else a distinct setup-failure label aborts) and the whole chain (mask-passthrough segments into primed zeroed buffers, eager final micro through DDP, SGD step) was re-verified bit-exact against the parent step and cross-rank identical on two-rank gloo DDP on the actual installed transformers, covering the gradient_as_bucket_view=True interaction where the reducer copies the presented non-view grads into its buckets exactly as it does for the parent's freshly allocated grads.

Numerics: the replacement preserves the exact kernel sequence, order, dtypes, inputs and loss scaling of the parent (the mask passthrough performs the same attn_weights + mask addition on bit-identical mask values; 0 + x = x in fp32 for the primed-buffer accumulation), the final synchronized micro-batch presents the reducer the same kind of defined non-bucket-view gradients it sees in the parent, and the 13 fp32 RING SUM allreduces, reduced gradients and SGD update are unchanged, so exact_gradient_replica_check (atol=0.0/rtol=0.0), global_batch_gradient_check, parameter_update_check, finite_loss and the corruption control behave as baseline. The captured segments contain no RNG (all dropouts are 0.0) and no collective, so replays are deterministic.

Step-time constraint: replay removes most CPU dispatch work of the first three micro-batches and adds only three small input copies plus one fused about-497.8 MB gradient zero (well under 1 ms) inside the timed region, so clean step_ms is expected below the parent's measured 139.96-146.20 ms AB/BA range against the 144.80321415 ms limit - unlike the previous trial, which failed at 145.55/144.25 while running parent fallback after its capture crash. Residual risk is parent-level machine noise on a degraded (fallback) run if an unforeseen GPU-only capture failure occurs.

Objective effect is bounded and honestly framed: the wire transfer itself is measured at its warmed floor (61.82 ms rank 0 / 62.90 ms rank 1, collective_calibration-1af5837f), so the expected improvement is only the arrival-skew/wait and overlap-contention component of the kernel durations, roughly 0.4-4.5 ms depending on the parent endpoint drawn (parent baseline samples 63.21-66.48 ms). If the residual gap is transport jitter or SM contention insensitive to CPU dispatch scheduling, this run acts as a measured control that empirically pins the in-contract floor; no wire-time reduction or general transfer-speed claim is made - the metric includes device waiting by definition, and acceptance requires every AB/BA pair to exceed its MAD-derived noise bound (2.58/4.54 ms last round), which the gain may not clear.

Coverage and evidence: CUDA graph replay does not re-run Python dispatch for the captured segment's inner operators; they execute as the same native kernels via graph launches (corroborated in traces by graph-launch entries plus the unchanged count of eager NCCL kernels), while the 13 allreduce_ calls, the final backward and the optimizer step remain eagerly dispatched and traceable. No inner call is eliminated (eliminated_calls is empty) and no consumer changes: the same accumulated gradients feed the same reducer buckets, the same allreduces and the same optimizer. Route labels are candidate self-report, not a substitute for the framework's output, coverage and trace checks.

Memory reporting: the retained gradient buffers and the graph pool increase reserved memory and the lifecycle peak counters; warm-run peak_allocated_bytes may decrease slightly as per-step autograd gradient allocations move into the retained buffers and the capture-time pool. These are allocator-counter effects under the frozen metric definitions, not the objective and not a claimed physical-memory saving.

No tunable parameters: a single deterministic configuration with an empty parameter_space, so the search cannot rerun this bundle with varying communication settings; the previous communication-side failure modes (rerouted communicator arms in trial-5a705e709d, functional-binding arms in trial-43f18a5360) cannot recur from this candidate.
